newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia awards prizes to coffee exporters.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia awards prizes to coffee exporters.

text.p: Ethiopian authorities have awarded prizes to 10 coffee exporters and two producing regions for exceptional performances in exporting a record 102,000 tonnes in 1995/96 (October/September).
Nine private exporters and the state-run Ethiopian Coffee Export Enterprise were given the prizes at the annual coffee exporters' ceremony presided over by a cabinet minister.

The awards were at a ceremony on Sunday but details and the minister's remarks were only made public on Tuesday. The prizes were mainly trophies such as cups and shields. It was not immediately known whether cash gifts were also awarded.

Of the total coffee Ethiopia exported in 1995/96, some 47 private coffee exporters sold 48,000 tonnes for about $141.8 million while the state-run Ethiopian Coffee Export Enterprise exported 53,183 tonnes for around $137.72 million.
Fantaye Biftu, minister for trade and finance in the prime minister's office, said the awards were "for a job well dome".
He urged exporters not only to satisfy existing markets but to make extra effort to look for new buyers. He promised the government would do all it can to improve the export climate.
Fantaye also commended Oromyia and the Southern Nations and Nationalities Regions -- two of Ethiopia's coffee regions -- for producing more coffee in 1995/96 than any other crop year.
He urged coffee growers to try and produce quality coffee which could fetch better price in the international market.
Nile International Trading Company and Ethiopian Coffee Export Enterprise were among the top prize winners.
The private Ethiopian Coffee Exporters' Association was also awarded a cup for outstanding performance and helping exporters to enhance their business.
The Association monitors market trends on the Reuters commodity service for its members to bring them up to date.
It also provides training and handles issues its members might raise with the govenrment or financial institutions.
Aschenaki GebreHiwot, secretary general of the private Ethiopian Coffee Exporters' Association said better information on international trends helped boost exports.
"This year's Ethiopian coffee success story could be attributed to the invaluable information exporters' received through Reuters commodity service," Aschenaki said.
Tsegaye Berhane, general-manager of the Ethiopian Coffee and Tea Authority, confirmed that Ethiopia planned to export 108,000 tonnes of coffee in 1996/97 crop year and earn $237 million.
He said predicted earnings were based on the forecast for reduced coffee price in the international market in that period.

Ethiopia exported 102,00 tonnes of coffee in 1995/96, the largest volume in its trade history but earned $279.5 million -- less than the $300.9 million it received for exporting 78,420 tonnes of coffee in 1994/95 --Nairobi Newsroom ++254-2 330-261.
